questions.question: The fundamental economic problem of scarcity arises because human wants are unlimited while productive resources are:
options: A) Controlled exclusively by international agencies
B) Freely available in nature without cost
C) Limited in supply and have alternative uses
D) Growing faster than population needs
questions.explanation: Scarcity arises because productive resources are limited relative to unlimited human wants and possess alternative uses.

questions.question: When Marginal Utility (MU) derived from consuming an extra unit of a good is zero, Total Utility (TU) is:
questions.explanation: Total Utility reaches its maximum point when Marginal Utility falls to zero.

questions.question: If a consumer buys two goods, X and Y, with prices \( P_x \) and \( P_y \) using income \( M \), the budget line equation is written as:
options: B) \( P_x \cdot X - P_y \cdot Y = M \)
C) \( X / P_x + Y / P_y = M \)
D) \( P_x \cdot X + P_y \cdot Y = M \)
questions.explanation: The budget line represents all consumption bundles that cost exactly the consumer's income: \( P_x \cdot X + P_y \cdot Y = M \).

questions.question: The Law of Demand states that, other things remaining constant, there is:
options: A) A direct positive relationship between price and quantity supplied
B) A constant expenditure relationship across all commodities
C) An inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded of a commodity
D) No relationship between market price and household purchases
questions.explanation: The Law of Demand establishes an inverse relationship between own-price and quantity demanded, ceteris paribus.

questions.question: If an increase in the consumer's income leads to a decrease in the demand for good X, good X is categorized as:
questions.explanation: An inferior good has a negative income elasticity of demand; demand falls as consumer income rises.

questions.question: Marginal Product of a variable factor is defined as:
options: A) The total monetary sales value of output generated by the enterprise
B) Total Product divided by total capital equipment employed
C) The change in Total Product resulting from employing one additional unit of the variable input
D) The minimum output required to cover total variable costs
questions.explanation: \( \text{MP}_L = \Delta \text{TP} / \Delta L \), which is the additional output produced by hiring one more unit of labor.

questions.question: Total Cost (TC) in the short run is the summation of:
options: A) Implicit Cost and Depreciation reserve
B) Marginal Cost and Average Revenue
C) Average Fixed Cost and Explicit Cost
D) Total Fixed Cost and Total Variable Cost
questions.explanation: In the short run, Total Cost equals Total Fixed Cost plus Total Variable Cost (\( \text{TC} = \text{TFC} + \text{TVC} \)).

questions.question: Average Revenue (AR) earned by a firm at any level of output is always mathematically equal to:
options: A) Total Cost divided by total sales
B) Market Price of the output unit
C) Marginal Cost multiplied by output
D) Total Revenue minus Total Profit
questions.explanation: \( \text{AR} = \text{TR} / Q = (P \cdot Q) / Q = P \). Average revenue is identical to price.

questions.topic: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.question: In a perfectly competitive industry, the price of a product is determined by:
options: A) The largest manufacturing firm in the industry
B) Industry market demand and market supply forces
D) Trade unions through collective bargaining
questions.explanation: The industry equilibrium price is determined by the intersection of total market demand and market supply.

questions.topic: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.question: Other factors remaining unchanged, a producer will generally supply more of a good when:
options: A) The price of the good itself increases
B) Taxes on the production of the good increase
C) Factor input prices rise sharply
questions.explanation: The Law of Supply states that higher prices offer greater profit margins, encouraging firms to expand output.

questions.question: At the market equilibrium price of a commodity:
options: A) Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied
B) Quantity demanded strictly exceeds quantity supplied
C) Quantity supplied strictly exceeds quantity demanded
questions.explanation: Equilibrium price clears the market so that quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

questions.question: A price floor (support price) set legally by the government is usually fixed:
options: A) At the prevailing equilibrium price
B) Below the market equilibrium price
C) At zero cost to retail consumers
D) Above the market equilibrium price
questions.explanation: A price floor is effective only when set above equilibrium price to guarantee minimum remunerative earnings to producers.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a capital good?
options: A) Milk bought by a family for daily tea consumption
B) A loaf of bread purchased by a household for breakfast
C) Industrial machinery installed in an automobile assembly plant
D) Petrol filled in a private family two-wheeler
questions.explanation: Industrial machinery is a durable physical asset used repeatedly in production over many years, qualifying as a capital good.

questions.question: Consumption of Fixed Capital is the official national accounting term used for:
options: A) Purchase of imported raw materials
B) Normal wear and tear and expected obsolescence (Depreciation)
C) Inventory accumulation of finished goods
questions.explanation: Consumption of fixed capital is the replacement cost of capital assets resulting from normal wear and tear and expected obsolescence.

questions.question: Net Indirect Taxes are calculated as:
options: B) Direct Personal Taxes plus Corporate Taxes
C) Indirect Taxes plus Export Subsidies
D) Gross Indirect Taxes minus Subsidies
questions.explanation: Net Indirect Taxes (NIT) = Indirect Taxes - Subsidies.

questions.question: When money is used to state the price of books, clothes, and automobiles, it is serving the function of a:
options: A) Unit of account (measure of value)
B) Store of value over decades
C) Standard of deferred payment exclusively
questions.explanation: As a unit of account, money provides a common monetary denominator in which prices and values are quoted.

questions.question: In India, currency notes of all denominations except the one-rupee note are issued by the:
options: D) Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India is the sole currency-issuing authority in India for banknotes; one-rupee notes and coins are issued by the Ministry of Finance.

questions.question: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to the fraction of deposits that commercial banks must keep as reserves with:
options: B) Foreign central banks in gold bullion
C) State government treasuries in bonds
D) The Reserve Bank of India in cash
questions.explanation: CRR is the mandatory percentage of Net Demand and Time Liabilities that commercial banks must deposit with the RBI in cash.

questions.question: In a two-sector Keynesian economy, Aggregate Supply (AS) is identical to:
questions.explanation: Aggregate Supply represents the total value of final goods and services produced, which identically equals National Income (\( Y = C + S \)).

questions.question: The relationship between Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) and Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS) is expressed as:
questions.explanation: Because any incremental income is either spent or saved (\( \Delta Y = \Delta C + \Delta S \)), \( \text{MPC} + \text{MPS} = 1 \).

questions.question: An annual government budget is an official financial statement showing:
options: A) Net foreign currency earnings of multinational banks
B) The private financial balance sheets of all listed stock market companies
C) Historical foreign aid remittances over the past century
D) Estimated receipts and estimated expenditures of the government for the coming fiscal year
questions.explanation: A government budget presents the anticipated revenue receipts and planned expenditures of the government for the upcoming financial year.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a Direct Tax?
questions.explanation: Personal income tax is paid directly by the individual on whom it is legally levied and cannot be shifted onto others, making it a direct tax.

questions.question: A record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world during a year is known as the:
questions.explanation: Balance of Payments provides a comprehensive accounting statement of all international economic transactions over a financial year.

questions.question: Foreign Exchange Rate represents the price of:
options: A) One domestic currency unit in terms of domestic consumer staples
B) One unit of foreign currency in terms of domestic currency
C) Gold bullion traded on domestic commodity exchanges
D) Commercial bank credit lent to agricultural cooperatives
questions.explanation: The foreign exchange rate is the price of one currency expressed in terms of another currency.

questions.question: On the eve of Indian independence in 1947, the occupational structure was heavily skewed toward agriculture, which engaged approximately:
options: D) Less than 15% of the workforce
questions.explanation: During colonial rule, nearly 70-75% of India's working population was dependent on agriculture for livelihood.

questions.question: The most significant and positive infrastructure contribution introduced in India by the British colonial administration in 1850 was the:
options: A) Universal adult literacy school program
B) Construction of rural tube-wells across arid districts
D) Establishment of heavy steel blast furnaces
questions.explanation: The introduction of the railways in 1850 by the British fostered internal geographical integration and commercialization of Indian agriculture.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the four common basic goals of India's Five-Year Plans?
options: D) Complete Abolition of Public Sector Enterprise
questions.explanation: The core goals of Indian planning were Growth, Modernization, Self-reliance, and Equity. Public enterprises played a central, not abolished, role.

questions.question: The miracle seeds introduced in the mid-1960s to initiate the Green Revolution were:
options: B) Traditional organic unhybridized heirloom seeds
questions.explanation: HYV (High Yielding Variety) seeds, combined with irrigation and chemical fertilizers, generated dramatic increases in farm productivity.

questions.question: The structural reform package initiated by the Government of India in July 1991 is commonly summarized by the acronym:
questions.explanation: The 1991 New Economic Policy centered around the tripod of Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation (LPG).

questions.question: As an immediate crisis stabilization measure in July 1991 to resolve the balance of payments emergency, India:
options: A) Devalued the Indian Rupee against major international currencies
B) Fixed the rupee parity strictly to crude oil barrels
C) Nationalized all foreign multinational banks
D) Banned all private agricultural exports
questions.explanation: In July 1991, the Indian Rupee was devalued in two steps by roughly 19% to stimulate exports and replenish depleted forex reserves.

questions.question: Which of the following expenditures directly contributes to building human capital in an economy?
options: A) Building gold bullion reserve vaults
B) Expenditure on corporate luxury entertainment suites
C) Speculative trading in precious gemstones
D) Expenditure on quality school education and preventive health services
questions.explanation: Investments in education, healthcare, and job training expand human capabilities, knowledge, and productivity.

questions.question: In rural India, the non-institutional sources of credit that traditionally charged exploitative interest rates include:
options: A) Village moneylenders and commission agents
D) National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
questions.explanation: Non-institutional credit agencies like local moneylenders, traders, and landlords often exploited peasant vulnerability with exorbitant interest.

questions.question: Workers who do not receive regular wages or salaries and have no social security benefits or job security are called:
questions.explanation: Casual workers are hired on a temporary, day-to-day basis without formal contracts, pension, or statutory medical cover.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-renewable natural energy resource?
questions.explanation: Coal is an exhaustible fossil fuel that cannot be naturally replenished within human timeframes, making it non-renewable.

questions.question: The People's Republic of China was officially established under Communist leadership in the year:
questions.explanation: The People's Republic of China was founded in 1949 following the Chinese Communist Revolution led by Mao Zedong.

questions.question: If the price of good X is ₹20 and the price of good Y is ₹5, the absolute slope of the budget line is:
questions.explanation: Slope of budget line = \( P_x / P_y = 20 / 5 = 4.00 \).

questions.question: When the price of a fountain pen falls from ₹50 to ₹40, the quantity demanded increases from 100 pens to 150 pens. The price elasticity of demand is:
When Total Product is increasing at an increasing rate, Marginal Product of the variable factor is:
questions.explanation: Increasing marginal returns mean each additional unit of variable input adds more output than the preceding unit, so MP is rising.

questions.topic: Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.question: In a perfectly competitive market, what are the two necessary and sufficient conditions for firm profit maximization?
options: A) \( P = \text{AC} \) and AC is falling
B) \( \text{MR} = \text{MC} \) and MC is non-decreasing (cuts MR from below)
questions.explanation: Profit maximization requires \( \text{MR} = \text{MC} \) and that the MC curve cuts MR from below.

questions.question: What happens to the equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity of wheat if an unexpected drought destroys a major portion of the standing crop?
options: A) Supply shifts left: price rises, and quantity falls
B) Supply shifts right: price falls, and quantity rises
C) Demand shifts left: price falls, and quantity falls
D) Both price and quantity remain unchanged
questions.explanation: A drought contracts the supply of wheat (leftward shift of supply curve), driving the equilibrium price up and lowering quantity.

questions.question: If Gross National Product at Market Price (\( \text{GNP}_{MP} \)) is ₹12,000 crore and Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) is ₹500 crore, Gross Domestic Product at Market Price (\( \text{GDP}_{MP} \)) is:
questions.explanation: \( \text{GDP}_{MP} = \text{GNP}_{MP} - \text{NFIA} = 12000 - 500 = ₹11,500 \) crore.

questions.question: If an initial cash deposit of ₹2,000 leads to total deposit creation of ₹10,000 in the banking system, the Cash Reserve Ratio is:
questions.explanation: Money multiplier = Total Deposits / Initial Deposit = \( 10000 / 2000 = 5 \). Since Multiplier = \( 1 / \text{CRR} \), \( \text{CRR} = 1 / 5 = 0.20 = 20\% \).

questions.question: If the value of the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) is 0.50, the value of the investment multiplier is:
The total borrowing requirements of the government from all sources (domestic and external) during a fiscal year are accurately reflected by the:
questions.explanation: Fiscal Deficit equals Total Expenditure minus (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts), measuring the net borrowing requirement of the government.

questions.question: A country experiences a Trade Surplus (favourable balance of trade) when:
options: A) The value of merchandise exports exceeds the value of merchandise imports
B) Foreign remittances received equal external debt servicing payments
C) Capital inflows exceed foreign direct investments
D) The central bank devalues the official currency value
questions.explanation: Trade Surplus occurs when visible exports exceed visible imports (\( X > M \)).

questions.question: In the pre-1991 period, why did private firms seek industrial licenses even beyond their existing production capacity?
options: A) To establish competitive joint ventures with small-scale village units
B) To transfer corporate tax deductions to rural farming cooperatives
C) To comply with mandatory export targets set by the WTO
D) To prevent potential competitors from acquiring permission to start production
questions.explanation: The 'license-permit raj' was often misused by large business houses to preempt licensed capacity and lock out new entrants from the market.

questions.question:
Arrange the following three countries in chronological order of the launch of their comprehensive economic reform programs:
1. India
2. China
3. Pakistan
questions.explanation: China initiated economic reforms in 1978, Pakistan began structural reforms in 1988, and India launched reforms in 1991.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is mathematically and theoretically TRUE concerning an indifference map?
options: A) Two indifference curves can intersect if the consumer has non-transitive preferences
B) An indifference curve is concave to the origin when marginal rate of substitution is diminishing
C) A higher indifference curve lies to the right and represents a higher level of satisfaction because more goods provide greater utility
D) The marginal rate of substitution is equal to the ratio of total expenditure across both goods
questions.explanation: Due to monotonic preferences, bundles on higher indifference curves contain more commodities, giving higher satisfaction.

questions.question: Suppose the Real GDP of an economy in the base year is ₹5,000 crore. If in the current year the Nominal GDP is ₹8,400 crore and the GDP Deflator is 140, what is the growth in Real GDP over the base year?
questions.explanation: Current Real GDP = \( \frac{8400}{140} \times 100 = ₹6,000 \) crore. Real growth = \( 6000 - 5000 = ₹1,000 \) crore, representing \( (1000 / 5000) \times 100 = 20\% \).

questions.question: In an economy, the consumption function is \( C = 40 + 0.8Y \) and autonomous investment is \( I = ₹60 \) crore. What is the equilibrium level of income, and what will be the new equilibrium income if autonomous investment increases by ₹20 crore?
options: A) Initial \( Y = ₹500 \) crore; New \( Y = ₹600 \) crore
B) Initial \( Y = ₹400 \) crore; New \( Y = ₹500 \) crore
C) Initial \( Y = ₹500 \) crore; New \( Y = ₹700 \) crore
D) Initial \( Y = ₹600 \) crore; New \( Y = ₹800 \) crore
questions.explanation: Initial: \( Y = 40 + 0.8Y + 60 \implies 0.2Y = 100 \implies Y = 500 \). Multiplier \( K = 1 / (1 - 0.8) = 5 \). With \( \Delta I = 20 \), \( \Delta Y = 5 \times 20 = 100 \), so New \( Y = 500 + 100 = ₹600 \) crore.
